channel.title: Mapping Forward
channel.description: Daily synthesis of articles on cartography, mapping, geospatial data, and geographic intelligence

item.title: Punjab to Digitise Property Records Through Drone Surveys and GIS Mapping
item.description: Punjab is launching a pilot project to digitise property records in 50 urban villages using drone surveys and GIS mapping technology to create accurate, transparent, and geo-referenced property documentation. — The Indian state of Punjab is embarking on a significant property record digitisation initiative, targeting 50 urban villages in a pilot project that leverages drone surveys and GIS technology. The project aims to create accurate, transparent, and geo-referenced property records that improve propert...

item.title: The Agent Drafts, a Human Approves: Inside State of the Map US 2026
item.description: State of the Map US 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin revealed three trends reshaping geospatial engineering: serverless map stacks replacing databases and tile servers with columnar files on object storage, AI agents drafting map data at industrial volume, and the deliberate human curation of sidewalk-level map data. — Key takeaways: Serverless map pipelines are shedding traditional databases and tile servers in favor of columnar files on object storage with parallel build steps ; AI agents are now drafting map data at industrial volume — from dashcam detections and satellite-derived geometry to automated validation of OSM contributions ; Sean Gorman's talk proposed restructuring OpenStreetMap tiles for AI consumption: embeddings, not pixels, as models now consume maps alongside humans ; Jeremy Herzog demonstrated restructuring the HIFLD critical infrastructure dataset for AI system consumption ("How We Prepared HIFLD for the Singularity") ; Sidewalks, crossings, and curbs — the fastest-growing part of the map — remain hand-drawn by the community, a deliberate choice the OSM community defends ; The guiding principle across all three trends: "the agent drafts, a human approves" — AI proposes, humans curate

item.title: TomTom Sees Breakthrough in Autonomous Driving Accelerating
item.description: TomTom expects partially self-driving cars to break through rapidly, predicting that by 2030 approximately 60% of new cars sold in Europe will feature systems capable of largely autonomous steering, acceleration, and braking on highways. — Key takeaways: TomTom predicts ~60% of new European cars sold by 2030 will have systems enabling largely autonomous driving on highways ; CEO Mike Schoofs sees 2026 as a transition year before revenue growth resumes, driven by automotive sector demand ; The company positions its map data and real-time traffic information as essential infrastructure for autonomous driving systems ; The prediction aligns with TomTom's CES 2026 focus on "mapping the road to autonomy" and powering the next era of driving ; TomTom's automotive navigation now combines predictive logic, a proactive AI agent, and integrated EV routing

item.title: Google Maps on Android Auto Tests Darker Theme to Reduce Night Glare
item.description: Google is testing a darker interface for Google Maps on Android Auto in beta version 17.6.663424, aiming to reduce screen glare and driver eye strain during night driving. — Google is currently testing a darker theme for Google Maps on Android Auto, available in the beta version 17.6.663424. The update addresses a well-known problem: standard dark mode on navigation apps can still produce too much light at night, causing glare that distracts drivers and reduces visibili...

item.title: Google Maps Has Become a Tool of Digital Imperialism
item.description: The Globe and Mail argues that Google Maps' compliance with Trump's Lake Ontario renaming order exemplifies how dominant mapping platforms have become instruments of digital imperialism, shaping how millions perceive geography. — The Globe and Mail's opinion piece frames the Lake Ontario renaming controversy as symptomatic of a broader issue: the concentration of mapping power in the hands of a few technology giants who can be influenced by political pressure from individual governments. Two decades after Yahoo Maps shut dow...

item.title: Apple Maps Renames Lake Ontario as "Lake America" After Trump Order
item.description: Apple Maps followed Google Maps in renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America" for US users after a Trump executive order, while MapQuest refused and Canada pushed back — highlighting how mapping platforms have become geopolitical instruments. — Key takeaways: Apple Maps renamed Lake Ontario to "Lake America" on its web version following a Trump executive order, days after Google made the same change ; Not all map providers complied: MapQuest explicitly refused to rename the lake and saw downloads surge 128% as a result ; Canadian government websites using Google Maps data inadvertently displayed "Lake America" and had to correct their maps back to "lac Ontario" ; The Globe and Mail published an opinion piece calling Google Maps "a tool of digital imperialism" ; Quebec government sites (Quebec511, SAQ, SQDC) and Ontario agencies (Metrolinx, HydroOne, LCBO) were all affected by third-party mapping dependencies

item.title: Why Ford Chose Apple Maps Over Google Maps for Its New EV Platform
item.description: Ford chose Apple Maps over Google Maps for its upcoming universal EV platform (Fathom) because Apple offered better integration with vehicle systems for range estimation, charging, and battery preconditioning. — Key takeaways: Ford selected Apple Maps for its universal EV platform, with the first model called Fathom ; Alan Clarke, Ford's VP of advanced vehicle projects, cited Apple Maps' constant improvements and engineering team flexibility as key factors ; EV navigation requires deep integration with powertrain systems: range estimation, real-time charging station availability, battery preconditioning ; Apple's ability to cross-reference navigation data with topography and weather for dynamic consumption predictions was decisive ; This is native integration, not CarPlay Ultra — Apple Maps runs on Ford's own operating system

item.title: Cities Are Giving Their AI Chatbots a New Dimension: Geography
item.description: Maricopa County and Washington D.C. are connecting AI chatbots to GIS systems, enabling residents to ask location-based questions like "What construction projects are within a mile of my house?" or "Is my property in a flood zone?" — Key takeaways: Maricopa County launched Mari (public) and Marco (internal) AI agents built on IBM Watson with Esri GIS tools ; The system uses RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for text search and Esri tools for spatial queries ; After testing 11,000 prompts, the system launched in June 2026 and averages 706 users per month with 12,000+ questions asked ; "Nearest neighbor" searches convert user addresses to map points and calculate distances to relevant services ; Privacy safeguards include policy warnings, access controls, 13-month retention limits, and guardrails against legal advice

item.title: HERE and Esri Bring a New Chapter in Location Intelligence
item.description: HERE Technologies and Esri are deepening their two-decade partnership to make location data a first-class enterprise IT asset, with a new location reasoning layer that lets AI interpret geospatial data without expensive model retraining. — Key takeaways: HERE and Esri are expanding their partnership beyond API-delivered data to persistent location data accessible through ArcGIS visualization and analytics ; HERE argues location data deserves recognition as a distinct discipline within enterprise IT strategy, not just another dataset ; A new "location reasoning layer" acts as an intermediary allowing AI to interpret location data without requiring full model training ; The partnership aims to bring Esri's ArcGIS capabilities to non-GIS users working with traffic, EV charging, and autonomous vehicle data ; Early assumptions that knowledge graphs and vector queries would suffice for AI integration proved insufficient — AI hasn't been trained on geospatial services

item.title: AMC Approves Citywide GIS Mapping and Digital Door IDs for Ahmedabad
item.description: The Amdavad Municipal Corporation approved a citywide GIS project covering 625 sq km with aerial LiDAR, 5,200 km of road surveys, 2.5 million geo-coded properties with Digital Door IDs, and a 3D digital twin — one of India's most ambitious urban mapping initiatives. — Key takeaways: Aerial LiDAR and photography will cover the 625 sq km municipal area with 240 ground control points ; 5,200 km of roads surveyed with Mobile LiDAR and 360-degree imaging; underground utilities recorded for asset management ; 2.5 million properties geo-coded through door-to-door surveys with Digital Door IDs for property tax assessment ; 3D digital twin with Level of Detail 3 models for 500 key buildings ; 12 GIS-based applications for town planning, disaster management, health services, and a citizen geoportal

item.title: MapQuest Refuses to Rename Lake Ontario, Sees Downloads Surge
item.description: MapQuest's refusal to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America" following Trump's executive order propelled it to the top of the US App Store navigation category, with downloads surging 10x above normal levels. — Key takeaways: MapQuest reached #1 in free navigation apps on the US App Store, with usage multiplied 50x compared to a normal week ; Sensor Tower estimates 184,000 global downloads for the week of August 24, including 162,000 in the US — 10x the usual volume ; Daily US downloads jumped 128% between August 26-30, and MapQuest also reached #1 in Canada ; MapQuest adopted the same approach as with the Gulf of Mexico renaming, which it also refused to implement ; The service, launched in 1996, was acquired by System1 in 2019 after passing through AOL and Verizon

item.title: Building AI-Powered GIS Applications: Key Technologies and Challenges
item.description: A technical overview of the key technologies — machine learning, computer vision, NLP, and cloud computing — needed to build AI-powered GIS applications that go beyond displaying analysis results to recognizing patterns and predicting future events. — Key takeaways: ML enables GIS to predict traffic congestion, identify flood-prone areas, and estimate agricultural yields from spatial patterns ; Computer vision processes satellite and aerial imagery for damage assessment, unauthorized building detection, and urban mapping ; NLP allows non-technical users to query GIS in natural language ("show me areas within 5 miles of a river with rapid urbanization in the last 10 years") ; Performance and scalability are critical: GIS apps work with satellite imagery, 3D models, and large geospatial datasets requiring cloud infrastructure ; AI automates routine GIS analyst tasks, freeing professionals for higher-value work

item.title: Summer 2026: Why Traffic Was More Fluid on French Roads
item.description: TomTom traffic data reveals that French roads were significantly less congested during summer 2026 compared to 2025, with the maximum congestion peak dropping from 35.6% to 29.4% and the number of high-congestion days in Île-de-France halving from 20 to 10. — Key takeaways: Maximum congestion peak in France dropped to 29.4% on July 7, 2026, compared to 35.6% in summer 2025 ; France experienced zero days above 30% congestion in summer 2026, versus 7 days in summer 2025 ; Île-de-France saw congestion peaks above 40% drop from 20 days (2025) to 10 days (2026) — a 50% reduction ; Key factors: shorter summer holidays, better anticipation of departure times, and trips spread across the entire season ; Declining purchasing power in 2026 also contributed to fewer and shorter road trips ; Gasoline consumption dropped significantly in May 2026, reducing state tax revenue

item.title: One Region. 40,000 Bus Stops. An OSM Map at Every One. — State of the Map 2026 × Paris
item.description: At State of the Map 2026 in Paris, T-Kartor and Jungle Bus present their massive OpenStreetMap-based project to produce and maintain location-specific area maps ("plans de proximité") for 35,000+ bus and tram stops across the Paris region — Europe's most extensive public transport network. — Key takeaways: T-Kartor, the Swedish cartographic agency behind Legible London, WalkNYC, and Toronto TO360, has partnered with Île-de-France Mobilités to create "plans de proximité" — stop-specific area maps for the entire Paris region ; The project covers approximately 35,000 individual bus and tram stops, each requiring a unique map with high quality and consistency standards ; OpenStreetMap data is the backbone: the process goes from editing OSM data to delivering print-ready files to transport operators, with dozens of intermediate steps ; Jungle Bus, a local OSM community organization, has been a key partner throughout the effort ; The talk at State of the Map 2026 covers the full production pipeline: context, build, deployment, maintenance, and lessons learned

item.title: Updated India Climate Opinion Maps for 2026
item.description: Yale's updated India Climate Opinion Maps tool visualises climate change beliefs, risk perceptions, and policy support across 34 Indian states and 634 districts, revealing sharp north–south divides in personal experience and climate literacy despite overwhelming national concern. — Key takeaways: The interactive tool maps climate opinions across 34 of India's 36 states/UTs and 634 districts using 25,000+ survey responses (2022–2026) ; After hearing a definition of climate change, over 75% of Indians in every state think global warming is happening, with rates from 80% (Andhra Pradesh) to 92% (Delhi) ; A stark north–south divide exists: northern states report higher personal experience with heat waves and perceived harm, while central/eastern states show low climate literacy (fewer than 50% in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal understand global warming is human-caused) ; Despite regional differences, 94% of Indians support national programs to teach about global warming and train people for renewable energy jobs ; The estimates use multilevel regression with post-stratification (MRP) combined with demographic, geographic, and climate vulnerability data, accurate to approximately ±7 percentage points at state level

item.title: München: Landshuter Allee Sperrung und ihre Auswirkungen auf den Verkehr
item.description: TomTom traffic data analysis reveals how the closure of Munich's Landshuter Allee for road maintenance sends ripple effects through surrounding neighbourhoods, with congestion levels rising dramatically in Neuhausen, Schwabing-West, Moosach, and Milbertshofen. — Key takeaways: The Landshuter Allee, one of Munich's busiest roads with over 70,000 vehicles daily, was closed for maintenance in both directions on consecutive weekends ; TomTom compared traffic data from August 13–16 (no closure) with August 20–23 (northern carriageway closed) to measure impact ; Neuhausen-Nymphenburg was most affected, but Schwabing-West, Moosach, and Milbertshofen-Am Hart also saw significant congestion increases ; TomTom's "Congestion Level" metric quantifies how much travel times increase in affected neighbourhoods compared to baseline ; The analysis identifies which alternative routes absorbed the additional traffic, demonstrating the value of real-time traffic mapping for urban planning

item.title: Nepal–Tibet Floods in Maps, Photos and Videos
item.description: A devastating flash flood triggered by a landslide on the Nepal–Tibet border has killed at least 168 people with over 1,300 missing, and ABC News uses maps, verified satellite imagery, and video footage to document the unfolding humanitarian disaster along the Trishuli River. — Key takeaways: A landslide approximately 12 miles northeast of the Rasuwagadhi border post triggered massive flash flooding in Nepal's Rasuwa district on August 27, 2026 ; At least 168 people confirmed dead and over 1,300 missing, including 65 American tourists and 39 Australians ; The US Geological Survey registered a 5.2-magnitude landslide event, initially misreported as a 4.4 earthquake ; Verified maps and satellite imagery show the path of destruction from the Gyirong border through Nepal's Nuwakot district ; The disaster highlights the critical role of crisis mapping and satellite verification in covering remote, rapidly evolving natural disasters

item.title: ¿Qué factores llevaron a que Arequipa tenga un mayor nivel de congestión vehicular que Lima?
item.description: TomTom's latest Traffic Index reveals that Arequipa, Peru's second-largest city, has surpassed Lima in congestion level at 69.5%, with drivers losing 154 hours per year in traffic — raising questions about urban planning in rapidly growing secondary cities. — Key takeaways: Arequipa ranks 8th globally in TomTom's Traffic Index with a 69.5% congestion level, higher than Lima's 69.3% ; Drivers in Arequipa lost an average of 154 hours in traffic during 2025 — equivalent to 6 days and 10 hours ; Arequipa's congestion worsened by 1.9 percentage points from 2024, while Lima's increased by 0.8 points ; Despite having less total time lost than Lima (154 vs 195 hours), Arequipa's congestion percentage is higher due to its smaller road network ; TomTom monitors traffic in 500 cities worldwide using anonymised GPS data from drivers across the complete road network

item.title: This Former PG&E Engineer Is Building a 'Google Maps for the Underground'
item.description: CivilGrid, founded by former PG&E engineer Josh Mackanic, has raised $26 million to build a unified subsurface mapping platform that aggregates data on buried utility assets — solving a problem that causes 200,000 utility strikes per year in the US alone. — Key takeaways: CivilGrid aggregates disparate data on underground utility assets, property ownership, and environmental regulations into a single mapping platform ; The startup raised a $26 million Series A led by Spark Capital, with participation from Afore, A*, Ford Street Ventures, SNR, and Energy Impact Partners ; A PG&E case study identified $60 million in avoidable paving costs across 1,600 planned gas distribution projects using CivilGrid ; The US experiences approximately 200,000 "utility strikes" annually because utilities only have visibility into their own lines, not competitors' infrastructure ; Mackanic envisions evolving the platform from data provision to automated permitting and infrastructure planning

item.title: TomTom Expert: Robotaxi Rollout Reveals Challenge of London as a Testing Environment
item.description: TomTom traffic expert Andy Marchant says London's complex street layout and evolving infrastructure make it an exceptionally challenging environment for robotaxi deployment, with high-precision mapping and live traffic data forming core infrastructure for safe autonomous driving at scale. — Key takeaways: TomTom's Andy Marchant identifies London's narrow roads, changing speed limits, and evolving street layouts as key challenges for robotaxi rollout ; Regulatory frameworks, liability models, and operating standards are still catching up to autonomous vehicle technology ; High-precision mapping combined with live traffic and hazard information is "core infrastructure" for automated driving, working alongside vehicle cameras and radar ; Location intelligence provides context "beyond the immediate line of sight" of vehicle sensors, making robotaxis "street smart" ; The same mapping data will be critical for UK government and transport authorities to plan and govern safe, scalable robotaxi deployments

item.title: Making Maps Cool: John Nelson's Cartographic Journey from CMU to Esri
item.description: CMU alumnus John Nelson has turned cartography into a creative public craft, building Esri's Living Atlas by day and teaching nearly 40,000 YouTube followers how to make compelling maps by night. — Key takeaways: John Nelson works as a cartographer and UX designer on Esri's ArcGIS Living Atlas team, building what he describes as "a high-resolution, constantly living and growing model of the world." ; His maps support multiple industries: national and local governments, construction and engineering businesses, and medical systems that use his maps for predictive health analysis. ; He creates educational content for almost 40,000 YouTube followers, 13,000 on Instagram, and 26,000 on Twitter, driven by the principle that "nothing teaches like teaching." ; Nelson majored in geography, earth science, and social science with a minor in art at Central Michigan University (BA 2000, MS 2004), combining analytical and creative training. ; His father Burton Nelson taught geography at CMU for 81 semesters (1966–2006), and the family's connection to the institution is multigenerational.

item.title: Google Maps sur Android : activez cette option pour ne plus rater de sorties en tunnel
item.description: Google Maps on Android can now use Bluetooth tunnel beacons to maintain positioning when GPS signal disappears underground, matching a capability Waze has offered since 2016. — Key takeaways: A hidden setting in Google Maps for Android enables scanning of Bluetooth beacons installed in tunnel walls, allowing the app to maintain accurate positioning when GPS is unavailable. ; The beacons use Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), consuming minimal battery, and once activated the setting persists for all future trips without further manipulation. ; Waze, also owned by Google, has used this beacon technology since 2016, giving it a long-standing advantage in urban tunnels over Google Maps. ; The beacon deployment, started in early 2024, covers a limited set of cities: New York, Chicago, Paris, Rio de Janeiro, Brussels, Oslo, Sydney, Boston, and Mexico. ; No timeline has been announced for iOS; the capability remains Android-only for now.

item.title: Comment Google Maps sait-il quels restaurants sont populaires ?
item.description: Google Maps predicts how busy a restaurant or shop is by analyzing anonymized location history data from users who have enabled the feature — no merchant input required. — Key takeaways: Google Maps displays real-time and historical busy-time data for businesses without receiving any information from the business owners themselves. ; The predictions are built from anonymized location data collected from users who have enabled "Location History" on their phones; when enough such users visit a venue, Google can estimate occupancy levels. ; The system also estimates average visit duration by analyzing users' navigation habits over recent weeks, and derives wait times specific to each establishment type (e.g., table wait time for restaurants). ; Users who do not wish to contribute data can disable Location History in their Google account or Google Maps settings while still benefiting from the aggregate busy-time information. ; The feature illustrates how Google leverages massive-scale passive data collection across its services to produce derivative products that appear to require no active user or merchant participation.

item.title: Measuring a Bridge That Never Stops Moving: Multimodal Lidar Maps the Cape Fear Memorial Bridge
item.description: McKim & Creed delivered a centimeter-accurate 3D survey of a 1969 vertical-lift bridge carrying 65,000 vehicles daily — without a single lane closure — by combining mobile mapping, static lidar, and ground-based survey control. — Key takeaways: The Cape Fear Memorial Bridge in Wilmington, NC, is a 400-foot vertical-lift span built in 1969, now functionally obsolete with 65,000 daily vehicles and a $1.1 billion replacement in environmental review. ; NCDOT required centimeter-accuracy survey data but prohibited any lane closure, direct deck occupation, or interruption of marine traffic — and the bridge has no shoulder for target placement. ; McKim & Creed combined three data sources: a Riegl VMX-2HA mobile mapping system driven at 45 mph, a Riegl VZ-600i static scanner from ground and elevated positions, and a ground-based control network set entirely off the span. ; Survey control was triangulated from safe ground positions, then propagated to the structure via static scans. Mobile data was adjusted using unconventional vertical features (guardrail faces, light poles) as tie-planes instead of standard flat road surfaces. ; Validation showed mobile and static point clouds aligning at centimeter level; the workflow is repeatable for any structure too dangerous, busy, or sensitive to occupy directly.

item.title: Dans les coulisses de Google Maps : 72 signaux de ranking et l'architecture derrière la recherche locale
item.description: A reverse-engineered Google binary exposes Geostore — the system behind Google Maps entities — revealing 72 ranking signals, 793 data providers, and an architecture connecting Maps to the Knowledge Graph and the broader web. — Key takeaways: Google's Geostore builds a canonical representation of each place from 793 data providers, with conflation mechanisms to resolve conflicting sources — not just a single Google Business Profile listing. ; The Oyster Rank system uses 72 named ranking signals including reviews, query volume, listing impressions, directions requests, Wikipedia signals, and road segment usage (25 are deprecated). ; The 72 signals are not "the Google Maps algorithm" — additional systems handle query understanding, semantic matching, candidate generation, geographic retrieval, and reranking in a multi-stage pipeline. ; Geographic search does not use a fixed radius: the candidate area adapts to query density and the user's environment. Removing geographic weighting shifts median result distance from 6.87 km to over 4,000 km while preserving ranking order, suggesting geography changes retrieval, not just reranking. ; Maps and web search are connected through Knowledge Graph MIDs and the Webref layer, which associates web documents with entities — a store locator page is not just a search result, it is evidence about the entity itself.

item.title: How Portcoast Is Rewriting Port Operations in Vietnam with Digital Twins
item.description: Vietnam-based engineering firm Portcoast is using an integrated digital twin platform combining bathymetric data, drone reality models, and live vessel tracking on ArcGIS to revolutionize port design, accident analysis, and 100-year planning across Vietnam's port sector. — Key takeaways: Portcoast built a digital twin of a port near Ho Chi Minh City that enabled accident simulation using captured footage ; The platform integrates bathymetric data, drone-captured reality models, and live vessel tracking on a single ArcGIS system ; Portcoast's engineering pedigree gives it mastery of reality capture: drones, laser scanners, lidar, and unmanned surface vessels ; At a grain port in Vung Tau, the digital twin simulated grain conveyor belt flows from vessel to warehouse ; The company covers the entire built asset lifecycle: surveying, feasibility, design, engineering, and construction supervision ; Environmental data, underwater surveys, and years of studies feed into the single ArcGIS platform for government presentations ; The digital twin approach goes beyond 3D models to include live operational feeds, IoT sensors, and camera systems

item.title: Ahmedabad Launches ₹240 Crore GIS Mapping Project for 3D City View Ahead of Commonwealth Games 2030
item.description: Ahmedabad's Municipal Corporation has approved a ₹240 crore citywide GIS mapping project to create a 3D digital model, geo-code 25 lakh properties, and map underground utilities — preparing the city for the 2030 Commonwealth Games while modernizing urban governance. — Key takeaways: The e-Governance Committee approved a modern GIS database for all of Ahmedabad at a cost of ₹240 crore ; Around 25 lakh (2.5 million) properties will be geo-coded in two phases: 9 lakh in phase one, 16 lakh in phase two ; The project covers roughly 625 sq km and will create a three-dimensional digital representation of the city ; Aerial surveys using drones and aircraft with high-resolution cameras will create the 3D city map ; Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) will capture precise depth and location of underground drainage, water, and storm water lines ; Every property will receive a unique "Digital Door ID" via door-to-door mobile app survey ; 360-degree street-level recording using vehicle-mounted sensors, similar to Google Street View ; The project will be executed by Genesis International Corporation Limited over two and a half years, with 5 years of O&M

item.title: Tactile Maps Installed at MSP Airport Ease Travel for More Than Just Blind Passengers
item.description: Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport has become the first airport in North America to install custom 3D-printed tactile maps with braille and textures outside every bathroom, designed in collaboration with blind travelers to improve navigation for passengers with disabilities and everyone else. — Key takeaways: MSP Airport is the first in North America to install tactile bathroom maps with braille and textured surfaces ; 146 bathrooms across two terminals require almost entirely custom maps — only two have identical floor plans ; The airport coordinated with its Travelers with Disabilities Advisory Committee to develop designs and symbology ; 3D printing with a local Bloomington company enabled quick prototypes and lower costs compared to traditional sheet metal ; No Americans with Disabilities Act standards existed for tactile maps, so MSP created its own standards from scratch ; Ken Rogers, president of the American Council of the Blind of Minnesota, served on the advisory committee ; Airport staff hope to share their approach with other airports, with Portland already expressing interest ; The maps benefit sighted travelers too, given the complexity of some MSP restrooms with multiple entrances

item.title: This Unity Asset Pack Allows You to Add Interactive 2D and 3D Maps to Your Games
item.description: Infinity Code's Online Maps v5 Unity asset pack enables developers to embed fully customizable 2D and 3D interactive maps with routing, geocoding, GPS, and elevation data from 16+ providers including Mapbox, TomTom, HERE, and Google Maps into their game projects. — Key takeaways: Online Maps v5 supports 2D and 3D interactive maps with elevation on flat surfaces or an interactive globe ; Elevation data sourced from HERE, Mapbox, MapTiler, and TomTom ; Supports 16+ map providers with 88+ map types including Google Maps, Mapbox, ArcGIS, Bing Maps, and OpenStreetMap ; Compatible with Built-in RP, URP, HDRP, and Custom RP; runs on standalone, Android, iOS, Windows Store, and WebGL ; Includes raster and vector tiles with customizable Mapbox and MapTiler vector maps, 2D/3D/billboard markers, and built-in clustering ; Full source code included with no dependencies, available at 50% discount ; Powerful caching system for raster and vector tiles, elevations, and custom data ; Supports WMS, WMTS, custom styles, and multilingual maps with or without labels

item.title: Around the Geospatial, 3D, and AEC Industries: Ancient Structures, Coastlines, and Digital Twins
item.description: Geo Week News rounds up three standout geospatial stories: lidar revealing 24,000–30,000 ancient earthworks in the Amazon, a 5,000 km Australian coastline hazard assessment, and how 3D printing is transforming digital twin creation for the AEC industry. — Key takeaways: Airborne lidar has revealed a previously unknown "Aquiry civilization" in Brazil's Acre state with 24,000–30,000 monumental earthworks ; Researchers estimate 1.25–3 million people lived in the Amazon region in the first centuries AD — more densely populated than today ; Engineering firm Hatch completed a first-of-its-kind digital mapping assessment of 5,000 km of Australian coastline for flooding and erosion risk ; 1.4 million Australian properties are already at risk of flooding, with annual event costs approaching $400 million ; The coastline assessment used statistical and process-based modelling for a state government agency to create a consistent region-wide hazard picture ; The third story explores how 3D printing technology is being used to create physical models from digital twin data in the AEC industry ; The roundup demonstrates the breadth of geospatial applications from archaeology to coastal engineering to construction

item.title: Coimbatore Corporation Geo-tags 1,500 OSR Sites in City
item.description: Coimbatore's municipal corporation has geo-tagged over 1,500 of its 2,702 open space reservation (OSR) sites through GIS mapping, creating a digital inventory to prevent encroachments and enable public access to land records. — Key takeaways: Coimbatore city municipal corporation has geo-tagged 1,507 of 2,702 total OSR sites through GIS mapping ; The title-change process has been completed for 1,771 OSR sites ; GIS mapping began in 2025, with around 500 parcels mapped in the initial stage ; The database includes ward and zone details, survey and patta numbers, approved plot numbers, layout plans, and encroachment details ; Drone imagery and field verification by licensed surveyors were proposed as part of the exercise ; Once online integration is complete, residents can verify whether land is earmarked as OSR and belongs to the civic body ; The initiative aims to protect public assets from encroachment and provide a consolidated database of reserve lands

item.title: Cofiroute Selects TomTom Traffic to Enhance Real-Time Motorway Operations and Driver Information
item.description: TomTom announced that Cofiroute, a division of VINCI Autoroutes and a leading private French highway operator, has selected TomTom Traffic and Route Monitoring to provide real-time traffic visibility, incident management, and driver information across its motorway network. — Key takeaways: Cofiroute, a division of VINCI Autoroutes, has selected TomTom Traffic for its motorway network ; The solution leverages TomTom Route Monitoring to monitor traffic conditions in real time on designated areas or routes ; Cofiroute uses the technology for incident management and to inform drivers via variable message sign (VMS) boards ; Traffic information can be published through road signs, websites, mobile applications, and other public channels ; Jérôme Pasteau, Head of Traffic Safety Solutions at Cofiroute, emphasized timely and reliable driver information ; Nicolas Durvaux, Operations Manager at Cofiroute, highlighted a consistent real-time approach across the network ; Benoit Joly, Head of Sales at TomTom, emphasized faster, more informed operational decisions for Cofiroute teams

item.title: Google Builds Korea Team for Full-Functioning Maps Service with Turn-by-Turn Navigation
item.description: Google is recruiting a senior partnerships manager in Seoul to build out a full-functioning Google Maps service in South Korea — including turn-by-turn navigation — following the government's February 2026 conditional approval to export high-precision map data. — Key takeaways: Google is officially recruiting a Seoul-based Strategic Partnerships Development Manager to build its Korea Maps team ; Google confirmed the plan includes turn-by-turn driving and walking navigation, currently unavailable in Korea ; The hiring follows South Korea's February 27, 2026 conditional approval of Google's export of 1:5,000-scale map data ; Korea had previously rejected Google's map data export requests in 2007 and 2016 over national security concerns ; Google Maps in Korea currently offers place listings, reviews, and transit directions but no turn-by-turn navigation ; Naver Map leads the Korean market with 29.25 million monthly active users vs Google Maps' 9.08 million as of April 2026 ; The new partnerships role will negotiate "first-of-a-kind" agreements with Korean companies and public entities ; Experts say Google needs better base-map data, POI/address data, and traffic/parking/transit information from local providers

item.title: New Floodplain Maps Take Effect This November in Larimer County
item.description: Larimer County, Colorado's updated Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) become effective November 27, 2026, incorporating new topography and hydrology data following the September 2013 flood, requiring county adoption to remain in the National Flood Insurance Program. — Key takeaways: Updated Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) and Flood Insurance Study (FIS) become effective November 27, 2026 ; The update is a response to the September 2013 flood and represents a proactive effort to update flood risks ; New topography and hydrology data have been incorporated into the updated floodplain maps ; Larimer County must adopt the updated FIRMs and FIS to remain in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) ; Property owners can check if their property is affected via the county's online resources ; Public hearing dates are available for residents to learn about flood insurance impacts ; The maps affect Unincorporated Larimer County specifically

item.title: Wildfire Map Spotlight: Colwash Fire, Washington
item.description: IQAir's wildfire map spotlight covers the Colwash Fire burning across Yakima and Benton counties in south-central Washington, which has consumed nearly 39,000 acres with only 8% containment as of August 24, 2026. — Key takeaways: The Colwash Fire spans Yakima and Benton counties in south-central Washington state ; As of August 24, 2026, the fire has burned 38,708.9 acres and is 8% contained ; Level 3 "Go" evacuation orders are in effect for areas in both Benton and Yakima counties ; Level 2 "Set" warnings and Level 1 "Ready" notices cover surrounding areas ; An American Red Cross evacuation shelter has been established at Prosser High School ; The fire affects areas near Mabton, State Routes 22 and 221, Glade Road, and Byron Hill Road ; Real-time air quality monitoring and wildfire maps are critical tools for public safety

item.title: Android Auto perd de nouveau les couleurs du trafic sur Google Maps
item.description: The Google Maps traffic color bug has resurfaced on Android Auto after being fixed on mobile, with users linking the disappearance of traffic lines to the Immersive Navigation rollout and finding no satisfactory workaround. — Key takeaways: Traffic colors (green, yellow, orange, red) have disappeared on Android Auto but work on the phone app ; The bug is linked to the deployment of Immersive Navigation, which introduced 3D buildings and visual enhancements ; The issue is server-side rather than tied to a specific app version, making it hard to pinpoint ; Workarounds include switching to overhead view, uninstalling Maps updates, or disabling auto-updates ; An Android Auto v17.5 user with Maps v26.33 still experienced the bug, ruling out a simple version fix ; Google has made no public statement about this dysfunction ; The loss of traffic colors significantly reduces Google Maps' value while driving

item.title: Google Maps : corrigé sur smartphone, ce bug handicapant touche maintenant Android Auto
item.description: After being fixed on smartphones and desktop, the Google Maps traffic color display bug has migrated to Android Auto, with users reporting that the Immersive Navigation update is the likely culprit behind disappearing traffic lines. — Key takeaways: The traffic color display bug has been fixed on iOS, Android, and desktop but now affects Android Auto ; Users report colored traffic lines (green, orange, red) disappearing on Android Auto screens ; The bug is confined to Android Auto — the same account works normally on the phone app ; The issue appeared after the Immersive Navigation update that redesigned Google Maps' trip display with 3D views ; No fix is currently available from Google for the Android Auto variant of the bug ; Users have tried clearing cache, reinstalling updates, and changing settings without success

item.title: Ordnance Survey Mapping Data Helps Identify Future Wildfire Risk
item.description: Britain's national mapping agency Ordnance Survey is using drone, aircraft, and satellite data to help government, emergency services, and businesses predict and prepare for future wildfire risks driven by climate change. — Key takeaways: Ordnance Survey (OS) provides mapping data to identify areas liable to flooding, wildfires, and other climate impacts ; OS operates a drone team of 21 pilots alongside aircraft and 200 field surveyors, achieving 2cm mapping accuracy ; More than 1.8 million homes are located within 100 metres of urban boundaries where most fires occur ; Firefighters used OS data during the New Forest wildfire on August 9, 2026, to plan routes and check gate widths ; OS monitors extreme heat, subsidence, winter flooding, and coastal erosion in addition to wildfire risk ; The agency checks new housing developments every two months during construction ; OS data helps emergency services decide resource placement, create fire plans, and identify at-risk homes

item.title: En désactivant l'historique de trajets de Google Maps, j'ai récupéré du stockage et ma vie privée
item.description: Les Numériques explains how disabling Google Maps' trip history feature not only protects privacy but also reclaims valuable smartphone storage space, with the function now storing data locally by default since 2024. — Key takeaways: Google Maps' "Vos trajets" (Your Trips) feature stores location history and movement data on-device since 2024 ; The function is disabled by default but can consume significant storage when activated ; Disabling it frees up storage space and eliminates personal movement tracking ; Users can set automatic deletion of trip history after 3, 18, or 36 months ; The feature does not share data with third parties by default when enabled ; Optional settings allow sharing trip data for ad measurement or experience improvement

item.title: Les Seychelles bientôt visibles en 360° sur Google Maps
item.description: The Seychelles will soon be visible in 360° on Google Maps through a project led by World Travel in 360 (WTI 360) with the support of the Seychelles Tourism Board, bringing the archipelago's main attractions to virtual visitors worldwide. — Key takeaways: The Seychelles will become visible in 360° on Google Maps through a filming project ; The project is led by World Travel in 360 (WTI 360) with support from the Seychelles Tourism Board (STB) ; WTI 360 will film the principal tourist attractions and scenic locations across the archipelago ; The 360° imagery will be integrated into Google Maps, making the Seychelles accessible to virtual visitors ; This initiative supports tourism promotion by allowing potential visitors to preview destinations ; The project continues Google Maps' global expansion of Street View and 360° coverage to remote destinations

item.title: Google Maps Bug Won't Show Traffic Data on Android Auto and More
item.description: A recurring Google Maps bug that strips traffic data from the map has resurfaced, this time affecting Android Auto users who can no longer see the green, yellow, and red traffic lines while navigating. — Key takeaways: Traffic data (green/yellow/red road lines) is broken for many Google Maps users on Android Auto ; The same bug was fixed in July 2026 but has returned, particularly affecting Android Auto ; Some map settings still show traffic data, but default navigation view is broken ; Google has not publicly acknowledged this latest wave of the bug ; Uninstalling Google Maps updates may temporarily fix the issue ; The bug may be linked to the Immersive Navigation rollout

item.title: Connaissez-vous My Maps, la meilleure alternative à Google Maps en voyage ?
item.description: Les Numériques explains how Google's little-known My Maps tool serves as a powerful travel planning companion to Google Maps, letting users organize multi-week trips with custom layers, waypoints, and shared editing — though it cannot replace Maps for turn-by-turn navigation. — Key takeaways: My Maps is a free Google tool for creating personalized maps with custom waypoints, lines, shapes, and thematic layers ; It excels at trip preparation on desktop: organizing stops, visits, reservations, and services across multiple layers ; Google Maps limits itineraries to 10 destinations, while My Maps supports up to 2,000 elements per layer and 10,000 per map ; My Maps custom maps are viewable in the Google Maps mobile app but cannot be used as continuous guided navigation ; Each waypoint accepts a title, description, hours, reservation number, price, photo, and link ; Maps can be shared by link and edited collaboratively, making it a geographic dashboard for group travel ; My Maps is not a reliable offline navigation tool; Google Maps' offline downloads remain necessary for driving

item.title: Celebrate 110 Years of National Parks with Maps, Search, and Gemini
item.description: Google showcases how its ecosystem of tools — Maps, Search, Gemini, and Ask Maps — can help people plan and enjoy visits to U.S. national parks during the 110th anniversary celebration of the National Park Service. — Key takeaways: National Parks Week celebrates 110 years of the National Park Service ; Search interest in hiking reached an all-time high, with "hiking for beginners" queries up 165% ; Rocky Mountain National Park is the top trending park searched alongside "beginner hiking" ; AI Mode in Search can help find hiking gear tailored to specific needs ; Ask Maps can suggest scenic stops, restaurants, and hotels for road trips ; Gemini Live can identify plants, rocks, and landmarks in real time via camera ; Acadia National Park was the top trending national park travel itinerary on Search ; Great Sand Dunes National Park is the top trending road trip destination

item.title: Hyderabad Ranks Fourth in India for Slow Traffic According to TomTom Traffic Index
item.description: Hyderabad ranks fourth among Indian cities with the slowest traffic, with a 10-km journey taking over 32 minutes on average, as vehicle growth far outpaces road network expansion according to the TomTom Traffic Index. — Key takeaways: A 10-km journey in Hyderabad takes an average of 32 minutes 37 seconds ; Bengaluru is slowest at 36 minutes, followed by Kolkata (35 min) and Pune (33 min); Mumbai is faster at 28 min ; Average vehicle speed in Hyderabad is 23 kmph, dropping to 5-10 kmph during peak hours and rain ; Commuters lose an average of 123 hours per year to traffic congestion ; Over 3,000 new vehicles are added to Hyderabad's roads daily ; Road infrastructure expansion has not kept pace with vehicle population growth ; The IT corridor (Gachibowli, Raidurg, Kondapur) sees heavy congestion from 9am to 11:30am and evenings until 9pm

item.title: Trump Shares Map Of Strait Of Hormuz As "New US Territory", Again
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump publie à nouveau une carte revendiquant le détroit d'Ormuz comme « nouveau territoire américain », illustrant l'usage politique des cartes dans le conflit avec l'Iran. — Key takeaways: Trump a partagé sur Truth Social une carte indiquant le détroit d'Ormuz comme « nouveau territoire des États-Unis » ; Le détroit est fermé par l'Iran depuis le 28 février, date du déclenchement du conflit ; Environ un cinquième du pétrole et du GNL mondiaux transitaient par ce chokepoint avant la guerre ; L'Iran déclare que le détroit restera fermé jusqu'à ce que les États-Unis « corrigent leur comportement » ; Trump affirme que les États-Unis ont « le contrôle total » du détroit, une affirmation contestée par Téhéran ; Cette publication intervient dans un contexte d'escalade rhétorique et militaire entre les deux pays

item.title: Google Maps : ce réglage discret préserve votre batterie en randonnée
item.description: Désactiver la vue satellite sur Google Maps en randonnée permet de préserver significativement l'autonomie de la batterie du téléphone. — Key takeaways: La vue satellite de Google Maps consomme davantage de ressources GPU et de données, drainant la batterie plus rapidement ; En désactivant cette option par défaut, un randonneur a constaté une nette amélioration de l'autonomie ; Le réglage est discret et accessible dans les paramètres d'affichage de l'application ; Cette astuce est particulièrement pertinente en zone de randonnée où l'accès aux charges est limité ; La carte standard reste parfaitement utilisable pour la navigation pédestre

item.title: The tax escape map: Billionaires are bolting for Florida from the West Coast and taking $29 billion in tax revenue with them
item.description: Une cartographie de la migration des milliardaires américains de la côte Ouest vers la Floride révèle un déplacement de 29 milliards de dollars de recettes fiscales, impulsé par les projets de taxes sur la fortune en Californie et dans l'État de Washington. — Key takeaways: Les cofondateurs de Google Larry Page (295 Md$) et Sergey Brin (275 Md$) ont quitté la Californie avant la date butoir du 1er janvier 2026 de la taxe sur les milliardaires ; Mark Zuckerberg (196 Md$), Jeff Bezos, Larry Ellison, Ken Griffin, Peter Thiel et Howard Schultz ont tous acquis des propriétés en Floride ; La Californie envisage une taxe de 5 % sur le patrimoine des milliardaires, visant 200 personnes pour 100 Md$ de recettes ; L'État de Washington a adopté une taxe de 9,9 % sur les revenus supérieurs à 1 M$, poussant Bezos et Schultz à partir ; La Florie n'a ni impôt sur le revenu ni impôt sur les plus-values, attirant l'ultra-richesse ; Indian Creek Island (« Billionaire Bunker ») compte 41 résidents avec sécurité 24h/24 ; Une carte des migrations montre un flux concentré vers Miami et Palm Beach

item.title: 7 Google Maps tricks I wish I'd discovered years ago
item.description: How-To Geek recense sept fonctionnalités méconnues de Google Maps, du repérage de stationnement au partage de progression de trajet, qui améliorent l'expérience de navigation au quotidien. — Key takeaways: Save your parking : Google Maps permet d'enregistrer l'emplacement de stationnement en tapant le point bleu de localisation ; Add a stop : il est possible d'ajouter des arrêts intermédiaires (essence, café) sans avoir à re-planifier l'ensemble du trajet ; Send directions to phone : un itinéraire planifié sur ordinateur peut être envoyé directement vers le téléphone via le même compte Google ; Set arrive time : Maps peut calculer l'heure de départ idéale à partir de l'heure d'arrivée souhaitée, et non l'inverse ; Download offline maps : télécharger une carte avant de perdre le signal garantit la navigation en zone blanche ; Avoid stairs : option d'accessibilité pour les trajets à pied, particulièrement utile pour les personnes à mobilité réduite ; Share trip progress : partage en temps réel de la progression du trajet avec un contact, s'arrêtant automatiquement à l'arrivée

item.title: Sir Anthony Hopkins Uses Google Maps to Revisit His Welsh Childhood Streets
item.description: Oscar-winning actor Sir Anthony Hopkins, 88, says he uses Google Maps virtually every day to revisit the streets of his childhood in Port Talbot, Wales, inspiring his first music album released at age 88. — Key takeaways: Sir Anthony Hopkins, 88, uses Google Maps to virtually walk the streets of his childhood in Port Talbot, Wales ; He describes going to streets and moving up the street using photographs on Google Maps "most days" ; The actor says he's "a bit too old" to physically return to walk the streets but finds solace in the digital exploration ; His childhood memories on Bracken Road in Port Talbot inspired a musical composition on his debut album ; Hopkins describes Wales as "the land of hiraeth (longing)" and credits it as the source of his identity ; He released his first album at 88, comprising music he has written over more than 60 years

item.title: Chhattisgarh Signs Two Key MoUs to Strengthen PM GatiShakti Implementation
item.description: Chhattisgarh state has integrated over 35 departments into the PM GatiShakti platform with 41 mandatory and 600+ additional GIS data layers, signing two new MoUs to strengthen geospatial infrastructure planning. — Key takeaways: Chhattisgarh has integrated more than 35 departments into the PM GatiShakti platform ; The state has mapped 41 mandatory and over 600 additional data layers on the platform ; 45 use cases and 30 analytical tools have been developed under the platform ; Two new MoUs have been signed to further strengthen GatiShakti implementation ; The platform uses GIS-based infrastructure planning for coordinated project execution across departments
